title: Republic of Upper Volta
capsule: The Republic of Upper Volta (République de Haute-Volta) was established as an autonomous territory within the French Community in 1958 and achieved full independence on 5 August 1960, inheriting boundaries drawn around the Mossi Plateau of the central West African Sahel. Politically turbulent, it experienced a succession of military coups — most significantly by General Sangoulé Lamizana (1966), Saye Zerbo (1980), and Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo (1982) — before Captain Thomas Sankara seized power on 4 August 1983 and launched a radical socialist and pan-African program of self-reliance. On 4 August 1984, Sankara renamed the country Burkina Faso ('Land of Upright People') to shed the colonial name. The country is landlocked, dominated by cotton and gold exports, and among the poorest in the world by per-capita income.
